issues.description: Entire compiled script is read into memory and shipped over RPC unconditionally, with no size bound.
issues.detail: The backend now does open(script_path).read() and returns it as script_content on every compile, even when the user never clicks Download. For large pipelines this is O(file_size) extra memory and bandwidth per compile. The invariant 'payload size is bounded by metadata' is broken. Either lazy-fetch on click via a separate RPC, or document and cap the size.

issues.description: File is opened without an explicit encoding, making decoding locale-dependent.
issues.detail: open(script_path) uses the platform default encoding. Compiled Python may contain non-ASCII identifiers or docstrings; on a server with a non-UTF-8 locale this will raise UnicodeDecodeError or silently mangle bytes. State the invariant: the script is UTF-8. Use open(script_path, encoding='utf-8').

issues.description: Download handler silently no-ops when content is missing; no feedback to the reader or user.
issues.detail: handleDownloadClick guards on compiledPath && compiledContent and then returns silently. If a future code path renders the icon while content is absent, the click does nothing and the user has no signal. Either hide the icon when compiledContent is falsy, or surface an error. State the precondition in a comment.

issues.description: Download icon is a clickable element but is not a button; lacks keyboard accessibility and semantic role.
issues.detail: GetAppIcon with onClick is not focusable or activatable by keyboard. The sibling Done indicator is an <a>; this should at least be a <button> or IconButton with role and aria-label. Readability for assistive tech matters here the same way readability for humans matters in literate code.

issues.description: Blob is created with type 'text/plain' for a .py file; minor mismatch worth labeling.
issues.detail: The compiled artifact is Python source; 'text/x-python' (or at minimum a comment stating why text/plain is chosen for download portability) would be more honest. Not a correctness issue, but the kind of small label that helps the next reader trust the code.

review.summary: The feature works but is UNDER-AUDITED on two fronts. Backend-side, the full compiled script is eagerly serialized into every compile RPC response with no encoding declared and no size cap — a payload-size invariant the prior code maintained is silently broken, and a non-UTF-8 locale will raise on decode. Frontend-side, the download path is functional but informal: a clickable icon without button semantics or keyboard support, a silent no-op when content is missing, and a slightly mislabeled MIME type. None are algorithmically wrong; all are the kind of small rigor a reader expects to see stated. Recommend lazy-fetch (or bounded) script content on click, explicit UTF-8, and an IconButton with aria-label before merge.
